decisions.statement: A flag's value is the argument after that flag.
A flag given more than once answers with every value that flag was given.
A flag nothing follows answers with a value that is not there.
A flag nothing follows is told apart from a flag no call gave.
The value of one flag is never read as another flag.
The flags a command takes are handed in rather than read from the command's page.
A flag the caller handed in no spelling for is refused rather than passed over.
A flag near a spelling handed in is refused with that spelling pointed at.
That refusal names the call as it was made and every flag that call takes.
A call handed no spelling at all is refused saying it takes no flag.
A message is read from the command line or from a file.
A call naming the message and the file the message is read from is refused.
A message is answered with the space at either end taken off.
A message that is empty once trimmed is refused.
One call bypasses the checks once.
A reason that is empty once trimmed is refused.
Nothing here acts on a value read.

definition: the values a command line has for the flags a command takes
